title: Salted Hash Enumerability Demo
description: Teaching demo of hash enumerability over toy corpora. Panel 1 hashes a chosen low-entropy identifier (month name, ISO country short name, or a synthetic plate ID) with bare SHA-256. Panel 2 runs a client-side dictionary attack over the same corpus and visibly recovers the identifier, with a candidate counter and elapsed milliseconds. Panel 3 commits to the same identifier under the estate's sha256-salted@1 shape: a fresh 256-bit crypto.getRandomValues salt, declared hash-excluded, is generated in the browser and withheld from the attack panel, and the same attack exhausts the corpus without a match. An honesty line states the boundary: the protection holds because the salt stays with the committer; a salt published next to the digest defeats precomputation, not enumeration. Toy corpora only; never presented as an eKYC compliance tool. No network, no storage, deterministic seeded example.

corpus.description: Toy corpus to draw the identifier from.
